summary: Tioga County steel lookout in Tioga State Forest: wooden USGS tower 1899, 47-ft steel tower 1921, removed about 1964 per register; no current site description found.

facts.status_note: Removed about 1964 according to the FFLOS register. No source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: U.S. Geological Survey erected a wooden tower on the site.
Planned repairs to the wooden tower until larger appropriation allowed a steel tower (Wellsboro Agitator, as quoted on the lookout page).
Forestry department ordered a 47-foot steel tower in August 1921 to replace the wooden tower it called unsafe. Erected by October 1921.
Register says the steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and replaced a USGS tower.
Fire warden Frank Davis, Jr. spent the fire season at the tower; tower was connected by telephone.
Fire on the Baldwin Run mountains (October 5, 1922) was spotted by the tower watcher; volunteers, including high school students, brought it under control within hours.
Coast and Geodetic Survey description of a survey mark at the tower, on state land. Whether the mark survives is not known.
Roads and trails cleared; fireplaces and picnic tables put in at the tower site for public use.
Wellsboro Agitator item gives the Baldwin tower as 50 feet, against 47 feet in the 1921 order.
Department list names Glen Fuller as towerman on Baldwin Tower.
Register says the tower was removed about 1964.
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1921 order and build reports give 47 feet (14.3 m), which is used here. A 1939 Wellsboro Agitator item gives 50 feet. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Newspaper items are as transcribed on the lookout page (Wellsboro Agitator and Gazette); the originals were not checked. The 1964 removal date rests on the register alone. Height conflict (47 ft vs 50 ft) is noted in the story. Brief access 'unknown' not upgraded: no source states whether the site is open now. The NGS survey mark (1933 description) may or may not survive; not checked. Brief record (14.3 m, Tioga State Forest, 2008 registration) matches the sources; no corrections.
